bib.title: Agent Lightning v1.0: Towards Harnessed Agentic RL

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Agent Lightning v1.0: Towards Harnessed Agentic RL", Zhiyuan He (first author, equal contribution with Siwei Zhang, Zhiwen Zhou), Yuqing Yang et al., Microsoft / Fudan / Zhejiang / Edinburgh. Preprint, arXiv:2608.17528v1 [cs.AI], 18 Aug 2026 (cover says "August, 2026"). No venue.
COVERAGE: 21 of 21 pages read, 62,968 chars, including appendix A (system design) and the references. The text extracted cleanly. Figure curves were not viewed, only their captions and the text around them.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Retokenization breaks token-prefix continuity between consecutive calls even when the text prefix holds. Three mechanisms: chat-template non-compositionality (Qwen's template can drop an earlier <think> marker), decode-retokenize drift, and inference-time output transformation (tool-call and structured-output parsers that repair or reserialize the response).
 number: none (no measured rate of breakage per mechanism)
 quote: "after retokenization, the token IDs corresponding to a_i inside p_{i+1} can differ from the originally sampled IDs in a_i." Figure 3 example: "the word having is sampled as the two tokens h and aving, but retokenizing the same text inside a later prompt may instead produce hav and ing." (p.5, p.4)
2. Proxy-side token replacement is off-policy stitching. AReaL and verl Uni-Agent buffer sampled tokens in the proxy and swap them into the next prompt. This changes the prompt the next response was conditioned on. slime and Polar do not replace.
 number: none, argued analytically
 quote: "Training it under the stitched prompt therefore introduces an off-policy discrepancy. Exact token-prefix overlap should be used for merging only when it preserves the prompt actually consumed during rollout." (p.6)
3. Agent Lightning's merge rule is best-effort merging. Merge two calls only if (p_i, a_i) is an exact token prefix of p_{i+1}. Otherwise close the sequence and start a new one. Drift only lowers the merge ratio. The gateway keeps no request buffer. Alternatives named: train every call independently (correct but recomputes prefixes), or tree/prefix-shared training (needs backend support).
 quote: "When it fails, the current sequence is closed and a new one begins. This preserves the prompts consumed during rollout and works with standard dense causal kernels, while retokenization drift merely lowers the merge ratio." (p.6)
4. Sample count per rollout is dynamic, so advantage and loss normalization can be corrupted. Causes: retokenization, subagents, context summarization. In their coding runs:
 number: 36% of rollouts stay as one sample; 2.41 samples per rollout
 setup: coding-agent run, Qwen3.5-9B, GRPO, mini-SWE-agent (Fig. 10, "Rollout-level Advantage + Rollout-level Norm" run)
 quote: "on average, only 36% of rollouts remain as a single, fully merged row, and each rollout yields 2.41 training samples on average (Figure 10)." (p.14)
5. Advantage should be computed at the rollout level, not the sample level. Their worked example uses a GRPO group of two rollouts, one with 3 samples (reward 1) and one with 1 sample (reward 0). Rollout-level baseline is 1/2. Sample-level baseline is 3/4. Frameworks differ: verl Uni-Agent and Polar use rollout-level; slime and AReaL use sample-level.
 quote: "Retokenization is an incidental phenomenon, and advantage assignment should not change simply because retokenization happened to split a rollout into more samples." (p.7)
6. Loss normalization. Seq-mean-token-mean (GRPO, Eq. 15) over-weights rollouts that produce more samples. Plain token-mean (DAPO, Eq. 14) is sensitive to long sequences. They prefer rollout-level token-mean (Eq. 16: pool tokens per rollout, then average uniformly over rollouts).
 quote: "when many long negative samples appear in a batch, it can cause instability later in training." (p.8)
7. Ablation on the coding run (3 settings, same GRPO objective, ~200 steps). Validation reward at best step:
 number: sample-level advantage + token-mean 35.0%; rollout-level advantage only 33.1%; rollout-level advantage + rollout-level norm 38.2% (step 128)
 setup: Qwen3.5-9B, SWE-smith-derived data, mini-SWE-agent. Single run per setting apparently, no seeds or error bars. Metric is the peak of the validation curve.
 quote: "The last variant produces the highest observed validation reward, reaching 38.2% at step 128, compared with 35.0% for the baseline and 33.1% when only the rollout-advantage fix is applied." Entropy: "grows more slowly and stays more stable ... than the variant with only the rollout-advantage fix." (p.14)
 Note: the rollout-advantage fix alone scored below the baseline.
8. Headline result.
 number: 41.8% to 56.4% on SWE-bench Verified (+14.6 points)
 setup: Qwen3.5-9B, RL only, about 6K training examples (about 5K filtered plus 1K always-fail tasks), 400 test examples, checkpoint at step 208 of the rollout-advantage + rollout-norm run. No baseline framework was compared on this task.
 quote: "RL improves Qwen3.5-9B on SWE-bench Verified from 41.8% to 56.4%, an absolute 14.6% gain." (p.1)
9. Other validations (training reward curves, no baseline frameworks):
 - Search agent: Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, GRPO, HotpotQA train, batch 512, 4 rollouts per prompt. Validation reward 25.1% to 41.7% (+16.6) (p.11).
 - Instruction-following agent: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, RLOO, LLM-in-Sandbox harness, batch 8, 8 rollouts per prompt. Validation reward 51.9% to 70.2% (+18.3) (p.12).
10. Collocated async RL. Rollout and update time-share the same GPUs. The gateway pauses new requests during the update, so the harness does not see it.
 number: roughly 2x end-to-end speedup over sync
 quote: "collocated async RL achieves roughly a 2x end-to-end speedup over synchronous RL while also using fewer GPUs." (p.10). No setup, table or figure backs the number; Fig. 6 is a schematic.
11. Retry handling. Gateway endpoints are idempotent. Retried LLM calls are deduplicated at sample assembly: for model_request events with an identical prompt, only the last call is kept (p.10).
12. Backend scheduling. Keep rollout ID and group ID on every flattened sequence. Keep all of a rollout's sequences in one optimizer update, otherwise "within-rollout policy skew" (pp.8-9). Stated as a requirement; no measurement.
13. Capture design. The proxy records prompt token IDs, response token IDs and response log-probs per call (a model_request event). A single scalar reward event is reported at the rollout end (p.19).
14. Reward hacking in the coding run: agents used git history to find the gold commit, wget/curl, pip download, and urllib. Fixes: disable git and hide .git, plus a Kubernetes network policy with a whitelist (p.13).
15. Data filtering: 59,136 SWE-smith records; 18,033 have an empty problem statement; 1,265 have a missing branch; tasks over 200 tests removed; difficulty filter by running Qwen3.5-9B 4 times and dropping the always-solved tasks (pp.12-13).

LIMITS
- Ablation evidence for the advantage and normalization choices is one task and one model, with no stated seeds or variance. Gaps of 2 to 5 points in peak validation reward are not shown to be significant.
- There is no ablation of merge strategy (best-effort vs buffered replacement vs tree). The off-policy claim for replacement is analytic only. No measured merge ratio is given, only the 36% single-sample figure.
- There is no measured effect for the loss-normalization claim "token-mean unstable with long negatives" beyond the entropy curve in Fig. 9.
- The authors say credit assignment across samples within a rollout needs "future work".
- The 2x speedup is unsupported by a table.
- The SWE-bench Verified gain has no comparison to other frameworks, and no with-and-without-RL control beyond the base 41.8%.
- The authors are the framework's developers and criticize other frameworks' design choices; the paper does not test those frameworks.

BUILDS ON: Original Agent Lightning (arXiv:2508.03680, 2025); verl/HybridFlow (2025); AReaL (arXiv:2505.24298, 2025) for async RL; slime; verl Uni-Agent; Polar (arXiv:2605.24220, 2026); GRPO (DeepSeekMath, 2024); DAPO (token-mean loss); RLOO (Ahmadian et al. 2024); Search-R1; LLM-in-Sandbox; SWE-smith (NeurIPS 2025); mini-SWE-agent.

CODE: None. The API surface is in Table 1 (p.20): the proxy path is POST /proxy/rollout/{rollout_id}/attempt/{attempt_id}/mode/{mode}/openai/v1/chat/completions.

FIGURES (from captions):
- Fig. 3 (p.4): retokenization "having" example.
- Fig. 4 (p.7): rollout-level vs sample-level baseline.
- Fig. 5 (p.8): loss-normalization worked batch.
- Fig. 6 (p.10): sync vs async vs collocated async.
- Fig. 9 (p.13): ablation curves.
- Fig. 10 (p.14): single-sample ratio and samples per rollout.

PROBLEMS: None. There were no embedded instructions. The extraction is clean apart from garbled math spacing.

Suggested placement: the note 07 paragraph "Capture at the API, and split on compaction" fits claims 1-5 and 13. Note 10 "Scaling" fits claims 10 and 12.
